François Le Gall # Ñ
Graduate School of Mathematics, Nagoya University, Japan

      Abstract
The subject of this talk is quantum distributed computing, i.e., distributed computing where the
processors of the network can exchange quantum messages. In the first part of the talk I survey recent
results [3, 4, 5, 6, 8] and some older results [1, 7] that show the potential of quantum distributed
algorithms. In the second part I present our recent work [2] showing the limitations of quantum
distributed algorithms for approximate graph coloring. Finally, I mention interesting and important
open questions in quantum distributed computing.
